Institute of Molecular Biology (IMB) Mainz Germany ([ROR:05kxtq558](https://ror.org/05kxtq558)) † Corresponding author ## Abstract Ribosome biogenesis is vital for sustaining stem cell properties, yet its regulatory mechanisms are obscure. Herein, we show unique properties of zebrafish meioc mutants in which spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) do not differentiate or upregulate rRNAs. Meioc colocalized with Piwil1 in perinuclear germ granules, but Meioc depletion resulted in Piwil1 accumulation in nucleoli. Nucleolar Piwil1 interacted with 45S pre-rRNA. piwil1+/- spermatogonia with reduced Piwil1 upregulated rRNAs, and piwil1+/-;meioc-/- spermatogonia recovered differentiation later than those in meioc-/-. Further, Piwil1 interacted with Setdb1 and HP1α, and meioc-/- spermatogonia exhibited high levels of H3K9me3 and methylated CpG in the 45S-rDNA region. These results indicate that zebrafish SSCs maintain low levels of rRNA transcription with repressive marks similar to Drosophila piRNA targets of RNA polymerase II, and that Meioc has a unique function on preventing localization of Piwil1 in nucleoli to upregulate rRNA transcripts and to promote SSC differentiation. ## Introduction The maintenance and control of the differentiation of adult stem cells are indispensable for living animals. In this decade, the relationship between the stem cell system and translation activity control has been revealed. Compared with that of differentiating progenitor cells, the global translation activity is relatively lowered in most adult and embryonic stem (ES) cells, and low translation activity is required for stem cells to maintain undifferentiated status (Ni and Buszczak, 2023; Saba et al., 2021). Despite this common feature of low translational activity, differences in the state of ribosome biogenesis (RiBi) have been observed across stem cell types. ES cells, hair follicle stem cells, and Drosophila germline stem cells (GSCs) are characterized by high levels of RiBi, whereas quiescent neural stem cells (NSCs) have low levels of RiBi (Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015). Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) have higher RiBi levels than differentiated bone marrow cells, but they have lower RiBi levels than their immediate progenitors, suggesting that cell type-specific mechanisms may regulate RiBi (Jarzebowski et al., 2018). In addition, phenotypes of RiBi defects in Drosophila GSCs appear to be controversial; attenuation of Pol I activity and the U3 snoRNP complex member wiched (wcd) mutant show premature differentiation (Fichelson et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2014), while knockdown of ribosome assembly and loss of DExD/H-box proteins (Aramis, Athos, and Porthos) that govern RiBi result in a loss of differentiation (Martin et al., 2022; Sanchez et al., 2016). Therefore, the mechanisms by which RiBi is coupled to low translational activity and proper stem cell differentiation are still obscure. By using an ENU mutagenesis screen to identify gonadogenesis defects in zebrafish (Saito et al., 2011), we isolated a unique mutant, minamoto (moto), in which germ cells arrest at the early stage of spermatogonia (Kawasaki et al., 2016). By whole-genome sequencing (WGS), we found that the moto phenotype is tightly linked to a mutation within a gene (ENSDARG00000090664) (Bowen et al., 2012), which encodes the coiled-coil domain-containing protein Meioc. Database analysis shows orthologs of MEIOC in vertebrates and most invertebrates, but not in Drosophila. The mouse MEIOC functions to maintain an extended meiotic prophase I with its binding partner YTHDC2 (YTH-domain containing 2), which is a 3'–5' RNA helicase containing an RNA helicase motif and YT521-B homology (YTH) RNA-binding domain (Abby et al., 2016; Soh et al., 2017). On the other hand, a Drosophila complex of bam (bag of marbles), a divergent homolog of Meioc sharing conserved amino acid sequences within the coiled-coil domain, and bgcn (benign gonial cell neoplasm), a paralog of Ythdc2 (Jain et al., 2018), plays a pivotal role in promoting stem cell differentiation (Perinthottathil and Kim, 2011). Although zebrafish meioc (moto) is orthologous to the mice gene, it appears to be functionally similar to Drosophila bam, making it interesting to see how it controls the development of germ cells. The present study revealed that zebrafish had spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) with low rRNA transcription, a characteristic that differed from many other stem cells, and that Meioc was required for upregulation of rRNA transcription and SSC differentiation. Independently of Ythdc2, Meioc regulated intracellular localization of the Argonaute/Piwi family protein Piwil1 (Piwi-like protein 1) that interacted with transcriptional silencing proteins, Setdb1 (Eggless) and HP1α (Cbx5). Our results suggested that low rRNA transcription maintained the undifferentiated state of zebrafish SSCs, providing a new insight on the relationship between the stem cell system and the RiBi control. ## Results ### Failure to differentiate spermatogonia in the zebrafish meioc mutant In fish testes, germ cells are surrounded by Sertoli cells within a basement membrane compartment and develop synchronously in cysts. Thus, the developmental stage of spermatogonia can be determined by the number of cells within the cyst (Figure 1A). Wild-type spermatogonial cells undergo nine rounds of cell division before entering meiosis (Leal et al., 2009); however, motot31533 mutant testes had only up to three rounds of division, containing 2–8 spermatogonia per cyst (Figure 1B). Mutant spermatogonia were positive for the undifferentiated spermatogonia marker, Plzf, which is expressed in single- to 8-cell (1- to 8-cell) cyst spermatogonia in the wild-type (Figure 1B; Ozaki et al., 2011), but negative for meiotic prophase I markers, Sycp1 and Sycp3 (Saito et al., 2014; Saito et al., 2011). Histone H3 phospho-S10 immunostaining indicated that mutant spermatogonia proliferated, but apoptotic cells were increased in the mutant spermatogonia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A). In zebrafish, mutants disrupting early stages of oocyte development become male (Saito et al., 2011; Houwing et al., 2007; Kamminga et al., 2010; Rodríguez-Marí et al., 2010; Shive et al., 2010). Similarly, no females and no oocytes developed in moto mutants (Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), as completion of the pachytene stage of meiosis I is a prerequisite for follicle formation (Elkouby and Mullins, 2017). By WGS and genetic analysis, we found that the motot31533 mutant phenotype was tightly linked to a mutation within the ortholog of mouse meioc gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Bowen et al., 2012). Fish harboring the motot31533 mutation inherited the moto phenotypes described above for more than 10 generations. Furthermore, fish homozygous for another allele, motosa13122, exhibited the same gonadal phenotype as motot31533 homozygotes, and motosa13122 failed to complement motot31533, confirming that these mutations disrupt the same gene (hereafter denoted meiocmo) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D). Both mutations encode a truncated protein that lacks the conserved coiled-coil domain (PF15189). We searched for paralogues of meioc gene using PF15189 domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) but were not able to find another gene in the zebrafish reference genome assembly GRCz11 (version 111.11). We then generated an antibody against the N-terminus of Meioc (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F) and could not detect the expression of truncated Meioc in the mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G). Zebrafish meioc RNA and protein signals were observed in a portion of 1- to 2-cell cyst germ cells in juvenile gonads at 25 days post-fertilization (dpf), adult ovaries, and testes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A). The cells exhibited a large nucleolus, characteristics of presumed GSCs in zebrafish (Kawasaki et al., 2016) and stem-type self-renewing type I germ cells in medaka (Nishimura et al., 2015). Both clear RNA and protein signals were detected in premeiotic germ cell clusters, and the protein was detected as granular structures in the cytoplasm with increasing sizes among cells until meiotic leptotene-zygotene stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C). ### Upregulation of translation is required for the differentiation of spermatogonia Since the global translation activity is generally inhibited in stem cells, we analyzed global translational activities of zebrafish spermatogonia using the O-propargyl-puromycin (OP-Puro) assay (Liu et al., 2012). In wild-type, we observed two populations, with low levels and high levels of de novo protein synthesis in 1- to 2-cell cyst spermatogonia. Whereas almost all large cysts with more than 32 cells (32≤-cell) of differentiated spermatogonia had high levels of de novo protein synthesis (Figure 1C and D). Almost all meiocmo/mo spermatogonia showed similarly low levels as that of 1- to 2-cell cysts (Figure 1C and D). These results suggested that some spermatogonia of 1- to 2-cell cysts had low translation activity in wild-type and that meiocmo/mo spermatogonia were arrested in the state of low translation activity. In order to know if translational upregulation is required for differentiation of spermatogonia, we examined the effect of cycloheximide on the development of spermatogonia in vitro. Cycloheximide decreased OP-Puro fluorescence intensities in differentiating spermatogonia in a dose-dependent manner in testis organ culture (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A). At 1.0 µM cycloheximide that reduced OP-Puro fluorescence to approximately 60%, BrdU incorporation decreased in 32≤-cell cysts of spermatogonia, while it was not affected in 1- to 4-cell spermatogonia (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B and D). We then examined the effect on differentiation of SSCs using a culture system, in which differentiation can be induced on the Sertoli cell line, ZtA6-12 (Kawasaki et al., 2016). After propagation of SSCs for 1 month, we transferred the cells onto ZtA6-12 and treated them with a lower concentration of cycloheximide at 0.2 µM, which reduced OP-Puro fluorescence to approximately 70%. The treatment maintained SSCs with a large nucleolus and not expressing Sycp3, whereas the control without cycloheximide showed expression of Sycp3 (Figure 1E and F). Bmp2 production of ZtA6-12 cells was not affected at 0.2 µM cycloheximide (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C), suggesting that the effect on Sertoli cell function was minimized. These results suggested that a certain level of translational activity was required for the differentiation of zebrafish SSCs. ### meioc mutants do not upregulate rRNAs in 1- to 2-cell cyst spermatogonia To estimate the state of RiBi, we examined the expression patterns of rRNAs and the ribosomal protein Rpl15 in zebrafish spermatogonia development. Interestingly, the signal intensities of 5.8S, 18S, 28S rRNAs, and Rpl15 were low in a portion of wild-type 1- to 2-cell cyst spermatogonia (Figure 2A), suggesting the presence of two populations also in the rRNA concentrations (low and high) in the 1- to 2-cell stage. We did not observe a low intensity of 5S rRNA. Those rRNA signal intensities increased in almost all 32≤-cell cysts and declined in spermatocytes. To distinguish between cytoplasmic and nucleolar signals, we performed fluorescence in situ hybridization of 28S rRNA. We found 1- to 2-cell cysts with low cytoplasmic signals also had low nucleolar signals (Figure 2B–D). Although cytoplasmic 28S rRNA signals increased to 32≤-cell cysts, the highest nucleolar signals were detected in portions of 1- to 2-cell cysts and declined at 32≤-cell cysts. These results suggest that 1- to 2-cell cysts contain populations with low and high rRNA transcriptional activity. ![Figure 2.](https://cdn.elifesciences.org/articles/104295/elife-104295-fig2-v1.jpg) **Figure 2.:** (A) In situ hybridization of 5S, 5.8S, 18S, and 28S rRNA and immunohistochemistry with anti-Rpl15 antibody in spermatogonia (gonia) and spermatocytes (cyte) in wild-type and meiocmo/mo. We next tested how rRNA levels were affected in meiocmo/mo and could not find cells with high signals of rRNAs and Rpl15 in meiocmo/mo spermatogonia (Figure 2A). We confirmed these data by performing RT-qPCR from isolated spermatogonia using the sox17::egfp marker. We have confirmed that sox17::egfp spermatogonia undergo self-renewal and differentiation into spermatozoa (Kawasaki et al., 2016), and the signal was predominantly expressed in 1- to 2-cell cysts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). Reductions in 5.8S, 18S, and 28S rRNAs in meiocmo/mo were observed (Figure 2E). Furthermore, the expression of the homolog of Drosophila non-LTR retrotransposable element R2 that transposes exclusively into 28S rDNA (Kojima and Fujiwara, 2004) was also decreased in meiocmo/mo. We next compared levels of unprocessed 45S pre-rRNA and pre-rRNA intermediates by Northern blot between meiocmo/mo and the wild-type. Each was normalized to 7SL RNA. In meiocmo/mo, the amount of 45S pre-RNA and the intermediates was reduced; however, the ratio of the meiocmo/mo to the wild-type was almost the same for 45S pre-rRNA and the intermediates: 0.69 (average 0.49/0.71, mutant/wild-type) of 45S pre-rRNA and 0.61 (0.72/1.19) of the intermediate with the 5’ external transcribed spacer (ETS) probe, and 0.33 (0.05/0.15) and 0.35 (0.17/0.48) with the internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) probe (Figure 2F). These results indicate that 45S pre-rRNA transcripts were reduced in meiocmo/mo, yet processing into pre-RNA intermediates was not affected. ### Meioc is required for demethylation of CpG in the IGS of 45S rDNA Features of silenced rDNA loci, DNA methylation, methylation of histone H3K9, and association of HP1α are known (Grummt, 2007). In eukaryotes, the transcription of each rDNA locus is regulated by DNA methylation and histone modifications in promoter and enhancer regions in the intergenic spacer (IGS) region (Santoro, 2005). Therefore, we examined DNA methylation state in the region. Since the regulatory sequence of rDNA was not identified in teleosts, we identified tandem repeats of 90, 127, and 318 bp in the IGS region of 45S-S rDNA (Locati et al., 2017; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), similar to carp (Vera et al., 2003). Unmethylated CpG in the tandem repeats was frequently found in isolated wild-type sox17::egfp spermatogonia, while it was rare in meiocmo/mo (Figure 2G). These results suggested that Meioc is needed for demethylation of CpG in the tandem repeats of 45S rDNA IGS region. ### meioc and ythdc2 mutants exhibit different phenotypes in the early stage of spermatogonia The YTHDC2 is a binding partner of the MEIOC in mammals (Abby et al., 2016; Soh et al., 2017). Zebrafish spermatogenic cells expressed Ythdc2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), and pull-down analysis showed zebrafish Meioc interacted with Ythdc2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). It has been recently reported that ythdc2 KO zebrafish lack germ cells (Li et al., 2022), but staining or expression analysis was not done to confirm that germ cells were completely absent. We separately generated ythdc2 KO zebrafish by the CRISPR-Cas9 system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), and observed that it had up to 8-cell cyst spermatogonia (Figure 3A). We observed that the number of 4- to 8-cell cysts was clearly different between meiocmo/mo and ythdc2-/-; the ratio of 4- to 8-cell cysts/1- to 2-cell cysts in the ythdc2-/- was almost the same as that in the wild-type, while that in meiocmo/mo significantly decreased (Figure 3B–D). Furthermore, ythdc2-/- spermatogonia contained both low and high levels of cells with 5.8S, 18S, 28S rRNAs, and Rpl15, similar to the wild-type (Figure 3E). The intensity of the 28S rRNA signals in ythdc2-/- was almost the same as that in the wild-type (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D). These results suggested that Meioc functioned independently of Ythdc2 on the differentiation of 1- to 2-cell cysts into 4- to 8-cell cysts. ![Figure 3.](https://cdn.elifesciences.org/articles/104295/elife-104295-fig3-v1.jpg) **Figure 3.:** (A) Histology (HE) and immunostaining against Plzf and spermatocyte markers (Sycp1, 3) in the ythdc2-/- testes. Arrowheads: undetectable Piwil1 signals in fibrillarin (green) positive nucleoli under the normal sensitivity imaging of Piwil1. ### Meioc interacts with Piwil1 and affects its intracellular localization To explore partners of Meioc on regulation of rRNA transcription, we performed LC/MS/MS for the Meioc-immunoprecipitate (IP) of SSC-enriched hyperplastic testes. The hyperplastic testes, which are occasionally found in adult wild-type zebrafish, contain cells at all stages of spermatogenesis. Hyperplasia-derived SSCs self-renewed and differentiated in transplants of aggregates mixed with normal testicular cells (Kawasaki et al., 2016). The results showed the enrichment of germ granule (nuage) components, compared with normal testis (Supplementary files 1 and 2). By immunostaining, Meioc colocalized with the germ granule components, Tdrd1 (Huang et al., 2011), Tdrd6a (Roovers et al., 2018), Piwil1 (Houwing et al., 2007), Piwil2 (Houwing et al., 2008), and Ddx4 (Houwing et al., 2007) in wild-type (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B). In meiocmo/mo, Piwil1 was strongly detected in the nucleolus (Figure 4A, arrowhead), whereas others exhibited the perinuclear localization characteristic of germ granules observed by Ddx4 staining as in the wild-type (Figure 4A). In contrast, we were able to detect low levels of Piwil1 in nucleoli of wild-type 1- to 4-cell spermatogonia with overexposed detection after the co-staining of the nucleolar marker fibrillarin (Figure 4B). The signals of Piwil1 in Ddx4-positive granules were decreased in meiocmo/mo spermatogonia, compared with wild-type (Figure 4C). We confirmed that Meioc interacted with Piwil1 by co-IP and revealed that Meioc-bound Piwil1 through the coiled-coil domain (Figure 4D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). These results demonstrated that Piwil1 has a property to localize in nucleoli and that Meioc interacts with Piwil1 in perinuclear germ granules. In addition, we did not detect the accumulation of Piwil1 in nucleoli in ythdc2-/- (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E). ![Figure 4.](https://cdn.elifesciences.org/articles/104295/elife-104295-fig4-v1.jpg) **Figure 4.:** (A) Immunostaining of Ddx4 and Piwil1, Piwil2, Tdrd1, and Tdrd6a in wild-type and meiocmo/mo spermatogonia. Scale bars: 10 µm. ## Discussion This study showed that zebrafish had SSCs with low rRNA transcription activity, and that increased activity correlated with differentiation. The state of low rRNA transcription activity is not similar to high RiBi of ES cells or Drosophila GSCs, but is closer to the low expression of ribosomal gene of quiescent NSCs (Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015). Since zebrafish SSCs have long-term BrdU-retaining cells (Nóbrega et al., 2010), low RiBi may be one of the states in quiescent cells, although quiescent HSCs have significant RiBi (Jarzebowski et al., 2018). Zebrafish 1- to 2-cell cyst spermatogonia had low and high nucleolar 28S rRNA subpopulations, and the high rRNA cells were not found in meioc mutants. Therefore, high rRNA is considered to be an activated state for differentiation. The progenitor 32≤-cell cysts had the highest translational activity and lower rRNA transcriptional activity than high rRNA 1- to 2-cell cysts. Our results also revealed that Meioc was required for the reduction of H3K9me3 levels and demethylation of CpG at rDNA loci. As shown in Figure 7C, Meioc prevented nucleolar localization of Piwil1. Piwil1 interacted with Setdb1, and both proteins could be found in the nucleolus. Furthermore, high levels of H3K9me3 and HP1α correlated with higher levels of nucleolar Piwil1. This is similar to Drosophila Piwi in piRNA-dependent gene silencing for Pol II transcribed genes (Jia et al., 2022). These data support the model that nucleolar Piwil1 interacts with Setdb1 in the nucleolus to maintain low levels of rRNA transcription via H3K9me3 and recruiting HP1α while Meioc promotes differentiation by blocking Piwil1 nucleolar localization and allowing rRNA transcription. The epigenetic state of tandem repeats of the zebrafish rDNA IGS region was similar to human silenced rDNA with CpG hypermethylation, levels of H3K9me3, and HP1α association (Grummt, 2007). The tandem repeats have been reported as enhancers of rRNA in Xenopus (Pikaard and Reeder, 1988), and the methylation status of the region is accompanied by rRNA synthesis (Bird et al., 1981). Since Setdb1 associates with Tip5, which is known to interact with DNA methyltransferase as a component of nucleolar remodeling complex (NoRC)(Yuan et al., 2007; Bersaglieri and Santoro, 2019), the Setdb1 that is interacted with nucleolar Piwil1 in this study is presumed to lead to CpG methylation in rDNA IGS region. The phenotypes of the zebrafish meioc mutants and ythdc2 mutants are different from those of mouse Meioc KO and Ythdc2 KO, which arrest at meiotic prophase I or immature follicles (Abby et al., 2016; Soh et al., 2017; Wojtas et al., 2017). In addition to different timing of phenotype expression between mice and zebrafish, the amino acid sequence of Meioc between mice and zebrafish is not well conserved (28.5%), while that of Ythdc2 is well conserved (65.5%). It is likely that zebrafish Meioc have different binding partners and regulate different processes of germ cell development from mouse MEIOC, causing the distinct phenotypes between these mutants. Many unique partners of Meioc, such as RNA-binding proteins, myosin proteins, Tudor domain proteins, heat shock proteins, and Cnot1, were found in the present study. In this study, we revealed the function of Piwil1 in regulating rRNA transcription. In Drosophila, nucleolar localization of Piwi and impairment of its localization by inhibition of RNA Pol I in ovarian somatic cells and nurse cells, and accumulation of undifferentiated GSC, delay of GSC proliferation, and upregulation of R1, R2, and rRNA transcripts in piwi mutants have been reported (Fefelova et al., 2017; Mikhaleva et al., 2019; Mikhaleva et al., 2015; Yakushev et al., 2016). In Caenorhabditis elegans, the nuclear Argonaute protein NRDE-3 binds to ribosomal siRNAs (risiRNA) and is translocated from the cytoplasm to the nucleolus, in which the risiRNA/NRDE complex associates with pre-RNAs and reduces the level of pre-rRNAs (Zhou et al., 2017b; Zhou et al., 2017a; Zhu et al., 2018). Therefore, Argonaute proteins appear to have a conserved function on controlling RiBi. This study showed that zebrafish Piwil1 used the analogous machinery for rRNA transcription as Piwi-dependent silencing Pol II transcription in Drosophila. Since Meioc was identified as a component of germ granules, the novel function of Piwil1 will open new insights into the interactions of germ granules and nucleoli to regulate RiBi and SSC differentiation. ## Materials and methods ### Zebrafish The motot31533 mutant fish were isolated in the Tubingen line by N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea mutagenesis screening as described (Saito et al., 2011). ## Review text

DOI: [10.7554/eLife.104295.3.sa1](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.104295.3.sa1)

Summary:

In this paper Kawasaki et al describe a regulatory role for the PIWI/piRNA pathway in rRNA regulation in Zebrafish. This regulatory role was uncovered through a screen for gonadogenesis defective mutants, which identified a mutation in the meioc gene, a coiled-coil germ granule protein. Loss of this gene leads to redistribution of Piwil1 from germ granules to the nucleolus, resulting in silencing of rRNA transcription.

Strengths:

Most of the experimental data provided in this paper is compelling. It is clear that in the absence of meioc, PiwiL1 translocates in to the nucleolus and results in down regulation of rRNA transcription. the genetic compensation of meioc mutant phenotypes (both organismal and molecular) through reduction in PiwiL1 levels are evidence for a direct role for PiwiL1 in mediating the phenotypes of meioc mutant.

Weaknesses:

Questions remain on the mechanistic details by which PiwiL1 mediated rRNA down regulation, and whether this is a function of Piwi in an unperturbed/wildtype setting. There is certainly some evidence provided in support of the a natural function for piwi in regulating rRNA transcription (figure 5A+5B). However, the de-enrichment of H3K9me3 in the heterozygous (Figure 6F) is very modest and in my opinion not convincingly different relative to the control provided. It is certainly possible that PiwiL1 is regulating levels through cleavage of nascent transcripts. Another aspect I found confounding here is the reduction in rRNA small RNAs in the meioc mutant; I would have assumed that the interaction of PiwiL1 with the rRNA is mediated through small RNAs but the reduction in numbers do not support this model. But perhaps it is simply a redistribution of small RNAs that is occurring. Finally, the ability to reduce PiwiL1 in the nucleolus through polI inhibition with actD and BMH-21 is surprising. What drives the accumulation of PiwiL1 in the nucleolus then if in the meioc mutant there is less transcription anyway?

Despite the weaknesses outlined, overall I find this paper to be solid and valuable, providing evidence for a consistent link between PIWI systems and ribosomal biogenesis. Their results are likely to be of interest to people in the community, and provide tools for further elucidating the reasons for this link.

## Review text

DOI: [10.7554/eLife.104295.3.sa2](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.104295.3.sa2)

Summary:

In this study, the authors report that Meioc is required to upregulate rRNA transcription and promote differentiation of spermatogonial stem cells in zebrafish. The authors show that upregulated protein synthesis is required to support spermatogonial stem cells' differentiation into multi-celled cysts of spermatogonia. Coiled coil protein Meioc is required for this upregulated protein synthesis and for increasing rRNA transcription, such that the Meioc knockout accumulates 1-2 cell spermatogonia and fails to produce cysts with more than 8 spermatogonia. The Meioc knockout exhibits continued transcriptional repression of rDNA. Meioc interacts with and sequesters Piwil1 to the cytoplasm. Loss of Meioc increases Piwil1 localization to the nucleolus, where Piwil1 interacts with transcriptional silencers that repress rRNA transcription.

Strengths:

This is fundamental study that expands our understanding of how ribosome biogenesis contributes to differentiation and demonstrates that zebrafish Meioc plays a role in this process during spermatogenesis. This work also expands our evolutionary understanding of Meioc and Ythdc2's molecular roles in germline differentiation. In mouse, the Meioc knockout phenocopies the Ythdc2 knockout, and studies thus far have indicated that Meioc and Ythdc2 act together to regulate germline differentiation. Here, in zebrafish, Meioc has acquired a Ythdc2-independent function. This study also identifies a new role for Piwil1 in directing transcriptional silencing of rDNA.

Comments on revisions:

Major and minor concerns were addressed in the revision.

results.result: The zebrafish meioc mutant exhibits arrested spermatogonial differentiation. Mutant testes contain only 2-8 spermatogonia per cyst (up to 3 rounds of division vs. 9 in wild-type), express the undifferentiated marker Plzf, lack meiotic markers Sycp1/Sycp3, and remain in an undifferentiated state.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C32, C51, C52, C54, and C60 provide converging evidence from histology, marker expression, and cell counts that meioc mutants fail to differentiate beyond early spermatogonia. The phenotypic characterization is well-documented with appropriate controls and multiple independent observations.

results.result: meioc mutant spermatogonia are arrested in a state of low translational activity. OP-Puro assays show that meiocmo/mo spermatogonia have low protein synthesis similar to wild-type 1-2 cell cysts, while wild-type 32≤-cell cysts have high synthesis. Cycloheximide experiments demonstrate that translational upregulation is required for SSC differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C64 and C71 are supported by OP-Puro fluorescence data and cycloheximide dose-response experiments. The cycloheximide experiments (C65-C71) provide functional evidence linking translation to differentiation, though the specificity of the 0.2 µM dose could be better characterized.

results.result: Wild-type zebrafish spermatogonia exhibit heterogeneous rRNA expression with low and high populations in 1-2 cell cysts. In situ hybridization shows that 5.8S, 18S, and 28S rRNA signals are low in a portion of 1-2 cell cysts and increase in 32≤-cell cysts. meioc mutants lack cells with high rRNA signals, confirmed by RT-qPCR.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C81 are well-supported by in situ hybridization, fluorescence quantification, and RT-qPCR data. The identification of two populations in wild-type and their absence in mutants is documented with appropriate quantification and statistical analysis. The use of sox17::egfp to isolate spermatogonia for RT-qPCR strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: 45S pre-rRNA transcripts are reduced in meioc mutants, but processing into intermediates is not affected. Northern blot analysis shows reduced amounts of 45S pre-rRNA and intermediates in meiocmo/mo, but the ratio of mutant to wild-type is similar for pre-rRNA and intermediates.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C86 are supported by Northern blot data with appropriate normalization to 7SL RNA. The quantification shows consistent ratios across different probes (5'ETS and ITS1), supporting the conclusion that transcription is reduced but processing is intact. However, only one biological replicate appears to be shown.

results.result: Meioc is required for demethylation of CpG in tandem repeats of the 45S rDNA IGS region. Tandem repeats of 90, 127, and 318 bp were identified in the IGS region. Bisulfite sequencing shows unmethylated CpG is frequent in wild-type sox17::egfp spermatogonia but rare in meiocmo/mo.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C92 are supported by bioinformatic identification of tandem repeats and bisulfite sequencing data. The methylation differences between wild-type and mutant are clear from the presented data. However, the number of clones sequenced and biological replicates should be specified for full evaluation.

results.result: Meioc functions independently of Ythdc2 in early spermatogonial differentiation. Zebrafish Meioc interacts with Ythdc2 by pull-down, but ythdc2-/- mutants show different phenotypes from meiocmo/mo: ythdc2-/- has normal 4-8 cell cyst ratios and normal rRNA expression patterns, while meiocmo/mo has significantly decreased 4-8 cell cyst ratios.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C102 are well-supported by pull-down assays, histological analysis, cyst counting, and rRNA in situ hybridization. The comparison between meioc and ythdc2 mutants is thorough and demonstrates functional independence in early spermatogonial stages. Statistical analysis supports the quantitative differences.

results.result: Meioc colocalizes with Piwil1 in perinuclear germ granules, and Meioc depletion results in Piwil1 accumulation in nucleoli. Meioc colocalizes with germ granule components (Tdrd1, Tdrd6a, Piwil1, Piwil2, Ddx4) in wild-type. In meiocmo/mo, Piwil1 strongly accumulates in nucleoli while other components remain perinuclear. Meioc interacts with Piwil1 through the coiled-coil domain.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C104-C115 are strongly supported by immunofluorescence colocalization, co-IP experiments, and domain mapping. The relocalization of Piwil1 to nucleoli in meioc mutants is well-documented with quantification. The interaction is confirmed by multiple approaches including co-IP with and without benzonase.

results.result: Nucleolar Piwil1 interacts with 45S pre-rRNA in SSCs. RNA immunoprecipitation shows pre-rRNA associates with Piwil1 in wild-type and is more enriched in meiocmo/mo. Pol I inhibitors (actinomycin D, BMH-21) but not Pol II inhibitor (α-amanitin) reduce nucleolar Piwil1 signals, suggesting pre-rRNA transcripts are involved in Piwil1 nucleolar localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C5 and C129-C133 are supported by RIP-qPCR data and pharmacological inhibitor experiments. The enrichment of pre-rRNA with Piwil1 is demonstrated with appropriate controls (IgG). The inhibitor experiments provide functional evidence linking Pol I transcription to Piwil1 localization, though the mechanism remains correlative.

results.result: Piwil1 interacts with Setdb1 and HP1α in nucleoli, leading to increased H3K9me3 and HP1α accumulation at rDNA loci. Setdb1 and HP1α are detected in nucleoli and interact with Piwil1 by co-IP. ChIP-qPCR shows higher H3K9me3 and Piwil1 enrichment at rDNA in meiocmo/mo (high nucleolar Piwil1) and lower enrichment in piwil1+/- (low nucleolar Piwil1).
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C9 and C135-C145 are well-supported by immunofluorescence, co-IP, pull-down assays, and ChIP-qPCR data. The correlation between nucleolar Piwil1 levels and H3K9me3/HP1α enrichment at rDNA is demonstrated across multiple genotypes. The ChIP experiments include appropriate controls and multiple primer sets.

results.result: Reduction of Piwil1 in piwil1+/- upregulates rRNAs and partially rescues meioc mutant differentiation defects. piwil1+/- spermatogonia show upregulated 28S rRNA in cytoplasm and nucleoli. meiocmo/mo;piwil1+/- spermatogonia differentiate to 32-cell stage and show increased 4-8 cell cyst numbers compared to meiocmo/mo, with the 4-8/1-2 cell cyst ratio reaching near wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C7 and C120-C128 are strongly supported by genetic interaction experiments combining western blot, in situ hybridization, histology, and cyst counting. The partial rescue of meioc mutant phenotypes by reducing Piwil1 provides compelling evidence for the antagonistic relationship between Meioc and Piwil1 in regulating rRNA transcription and differentiation.

results.result: Meioc expression correlates with rRNA upregulation and inhibits Piwil1 nucleolar localization. In isolated sox17::egfp spermatogonia, Meioc expression ranges from barely detectable to >51 granules. 28S rRNA intensity increases in cells with 11-50 Meioc granules. Piwil1 levels are constant across cells except those with 51≤ nuclear Meioc. Nucleolar Piwil1 is observed in cells with 11-50 Meioc granules but not in cells with 51≤ Meioc granules.
results.evaluation: Claims C146-C155 are supported by quantitative analysis of Meioc, 28S rRNA, and Piwil1 in isolated cells and tissue sections. The correlation between Meioc expression levels and rRNA upregulation is well-documented. The inverse relationship between high Meioc and nucleolar Piwil1 supports the proposed mechanism, though the analysis is correlative rather than causal.

results.result: meioc-/- spermatogonia exhibit high levels of H3K9me3 and methylated CpG in the 45S-rDNA region. Meioc is required for reduction of H3K9me3 levels and demethylation of CpG at rDNA loci.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C11 and C165-C166 are supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing increased H3K9me3 at rDNA loci in meioc mutants and bisulfite sequencing showing increased CpG methylation. These findings are consistent with the proposed model of Meioc preventing Piwil1-mediated silencing of rDNA.

results.result: Zebrafish SSCs maintain low rRNA transcription with repressive marks, and Meioc promotes differentiation by preventing Piwil1 nucleolar localization to upregulate rRNA transcripts. The model proposes that nucleolar Piwil1 interacts with Setdb1 to maintain low rRNA transcription via H3K9me3 and HP1α recruitment, while Meioc blocks Piwil1 nucleolar localization to allow rRNA transcription and SSC differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C14, C43-C45, C49, C156, C170-C171 represent the main conclusions synthesizing multiple lines of evidence. The model is well-supported by the collective data on rRNA expression, Piwil1 localization, epigenetic modifications, and genetic interactions. However, some mechanistic details remain to be fully elucidated, such as how Meioc prevents Piwil1 nucleolar localization.

results.result: The minamoto (moto) mutant was isolated by ENU mutagenesis and mapped to the meioc gene (ENSDARG00000090664) encoding a coiled-coil domain protein. MEIOC orthologs are found in vertebrates and most invertebrates but not Drosophila. Zebrafish meioc is orthologous to the mouse gene.
results.evaluation: Claims C31, C33-C35, C41 are supported by genetic mapping, whole-genome sequencing, and database analysis. The identification of the causative gene is confirmed by multiple alleles and complementation testing. The phylogenetic distribution is based on database searches.

results.result: meioc mutant spermatogonia proliferate but show increased apoptosis. No females or oocytes develop in moto mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C56 and C58 are supported by Histone H3 phospho-S10 staining, TUNEL assays, and histological analysis. The sex determination phenotype is consistent with other zebrafish mutants disrupting early oogenesis.

results.result: LC/MS/MS of Meioc immunoprecipitates from SSC-enriched hyperplastic testes showed enrichment of germ granule components. Many unique Meioc partners including RNA-binding proteins, myosin proteins, Tudor domain proteins, heat shock proteins, and Cnot1 were identified.
results.evaluation: Claims C103, C181, C188 are supported by mass spectrometry data. The enrichment of germ granule components is consistent with the colocalization studies. However, the functional significance of many identified partners remains to be determined.

results.result: Piwil1 accumulation in nucleoli was not detected in ythdc2-/-. Small RNA production is similar between meiocmo/mo and meioc+/mo testes, though small RNAs derived from rRNAs and R2 transposon decrease in meiocmo/mo, likely due to low rRNA expression. Meioc does not critically affect small RNA generation.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C119 are supported by immunofluorescence and small RNA sequencing data. The conclusion that Meioc does not critically affect small RNA generation is reasonable given the similar overall abundance, though the decreased rRNA-derived small RNAs are appropriately attributed to reduced rRNA expression.

results.result: Zebrafish meioc and ythdc2 mutants differ from mouse knockouts, which arrest at meiotic prophase I. The amino acid sequence of Meioc is poorly conserved between mice and zebrafish (28.5%) while Ythdc2 is well conserved (65.5%). Zebrafish Meioc likely has different binding partners and regulates different processes than mouse MEIOC.
results.evaluation: Claims C177-C180 are supported by phenotypic comparisons and sequence analysis. The hypothesis that zebrafish Meioc has different functions is reasonable given the sequence divergence and phenotypic differences, though this remains speculative.

results.result: Background on ribosome biogenesis in stem cells: RiBi is vital for stem cells but regulatory mechanisms are obscure. Translation activity is low in most stem cells. Different stem cell types show varying RiBi levels (high in ES cells, hair follicle stem cells, Drosophila GSCs; low in quiescent NSCs; intermediate in HSCs). RiBi defects in Drosophila GSCs show controversial phenotypes. Mechanisms coupling RiBi to translation and differentiation remain obscure.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C30 represent literature review and background knowledge, appropriately cited. These establish the context for the current study and identify knowledge gaps.

results.result: Background on MEIOC and related proteins: Mouse MEIOC functions with YTHDC2 to maintain extended meiotic prophase I. Drosophila bam-bgcn complex promotes stem cell differentiation. Zebrafish meioc appears functionally similar to Drosophila bam despite being orthologous to mouse MEIOC.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C40 and C42 represent literature review with appropriate citations. The functional similarity between zebrafish meioc and Drosophila bam (C42) is an inference supported by the phenotypic data presented in the paper.

results.result: Background information and technical details: Wild-type spermatogonia undergo 9 rounds of division before meiosis. Plzf is expressed in 1-8 cell cyst spermatogonia. Zebrafish mutants disrupting early oogenesis become male. Completion of pachytene is required for follicle formation. 5S rRNA low intensity was not observed. Drosophila R2 transposes into 28S rDNA. Features of silenced rDNA include DNA methylation, H3K9me3, and HP1α. rDNA transcription is regulated by modifications in the IGS region. YTHDC2 is a MEIOC binding partner in mammals.
results.evaluation: Claims C50, C53, C57, C59, C74, C82-C83, C87-C88, C93 represent cited background information, technical observations, or established knowledge that provide context for the experimental findings.

results.result: Discussion and comparative analysis: Zebrafish SSC low rRNA state is similar to quiescent NSCs rather than high RiBi stem cells. Zebrafish SSCs have long-term BrdU-retaining cells. The epigenetic state of zebrafish rDNA IGS is similar to human silenced rDNA. Tandem repeats function as enhancers in Xenopus. Setdb1 associates with Tip5/NoRC. Drosophila Piwi and C. elegans NRDE-3 have conserved functions in controlling RiBi. Zebrafish Piwil1 uses analogous machinery to Drosophila Piwi-dependent silencing.
results.evaluation: Claims C134, C157-C160, C172-C176, C182-C187 represent discussion points comparing the findings to other systems and proposing mechanistic connections. These are appropriately cited and represent reasonable interpretations of the data in broader context.

results.result: Summary and implications: Zebrafish 1-2 cell cyst spermatogonia have low and high rRNA subpopulations; high rRNA cells are absent in meioc mutants and represent an activated state for differentiation. Progenitor 32≤-cell cysts have highest translational activity but lower rRNA transcriptional activity than high rRNA 1-2 cell cysts. The novel function of Piwil1 will provide insights into germ granule-nucleolus interactions regulating RiBi and SSC differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C161-C164 and C189 represent summary statements and implications of the findings. These are supported by the collective data, though C189 is somewhat speculative about future insights.

results.result: Cycloheximide dose-response experiments: Cycloheximide decreases OP-Puro fluorescence in differentiating spermatogonia dose-dependently. At 1.0 µM, BrdU incorporation decreases in 32≤-cell cysts but not 1-4 cell spermatogonia. At 0.2 µM, cycloheximide maintains SSCs without Sycp3 expression, while controls show Sycp3 expression. Bmp2 production by Sertoli cells is not affected at 0.2 µM.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C70 are supported by dose-response experiments, BrdU incorporation assays, and Bmp2 western blots. These experiments establish that translational activity is required for differentiation and validate the experimental conditions used.

results.result: The meioc mutant exhibits arrested spermatogonial differentiation, with germ cells remaining undifferentiated at early spermatogonial stages (1-8 cell cysts), failing to upregulate rRNAs, and not progressing to meiosis as indicated by absence of meiotic markers.
results.evaluation: All reviewers affirm this core finding. Reviewer 1 states the data is 'compelling' and 'it is clear that in the absence of meioc, PiwiL1 translocates in to the nucleolus and results in down regulation of rRNA transcription.' Reviewer 2 notes 'Meioc is required to upregulate rRNA transcription and promote differentiation of spermatogonial stem cells' and Reviewer 3 confirms 'the authors provide convincing evidence that Meioc antagonizes Piwil1, which downregulates the 45S pre-rRNA synthesis.'

results.result: Wild-type zebrafish spermatogonia show heterogeneous translation activity, with 1-2 cell cysts having low protein synthesis and 32≤-cell cysts having high synthesis; meioc mutants are arrested in a low translation state, and cycloheximide experiments demonstrate that translational activity is required for SSC differentiation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The authors show that upregulated protein synthesis is required to support spermatogonial stem cells' differentiation into multi-celled cysts.' The OP-Puro and cycloheximide data are not questioned by any reviewer.

results.result: Wild-type 1-2 cell spermatogonia contain two populations with low and high rRNA levels (5.8S, 18S, 28S, Rpl15), with rRNA increasing in 32≤-cell cysts; meioc mutants lack the high rRNA population and show reduced rRNA levels by in situ hybridization and RT-qPCR.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these rRNA expression data. Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'Most of the experimental data provided in this paper is compelling' and specifically notes the rRNA downregulation in meioc mutants. Reviewer 2 confirms 'Meioc is required for this upregulated protein synthesis and for increasing rRNA transcription.'

results.result: Northern blot analysis shows that 45S pre-rRNA and processing intermediates are reduced in meioc mutants, but the ratio of pre-rRNA to intermediates remains similar to wild-type, indicating transcription is reduced but processing is unaffected.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without objection. The Northern blot data supporting reduced transcription but normal processing is consistent with the overall model and is not questioned by any reviewer.

results.result: Tandem repeats (90, 127, 318 bp) in the IGS region of 45S rDNA show frequent unmethylated CpG in wild-type spermatogonia but rare unmethylated CpG in meioc mutants, suggesting Meioc is required for demethylation of these regulatory regions.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the DNA methylation data. Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors nicely provided the molecular evidence on the antagonism of Meioc to Piwil1 in the rRNA synthesis' which includes the epigenetic modifications. No reviewer challenges the bisulfite sequencing results.

results.result: Meioc colocalizes with germ granule components (Piwil1, Piwil2, Tdrd1, Tdrd6a, Ddx4) in wild-type perinuclear germ granules and interacts with Piwil1 through its coiled-coil domain; in meioc mutants, Piwil1 accumulates strongly in nucleoli while other germ granule components remain perinuclear.
results.evaluation: All reviewers affirm this key finding. Reviewer 1 states 'it is clear that in the absence of meioc, PiwiL1 translocates in to the nucleolus.' Reviewer 2 notes 'Loss of Meioc increases Piwil1 localization to the nucleolus.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'Meioc sequesters Piwil1...to the perinuclear bodies.' The colocalization and co-IP data are accepted without challenge.

results.result: Nucleolar Piwil1 interacts with 45S pre-rRNA as shown by RNA immunoprecipitation (enriched in meioc mutants vs wild-type), and Pol I inhibitors (actinomycin D, BMH-21) but not Pol II inhibitor (α-amanitin) reduce nucleolar Piwil1 localization, indicating pre-rRNA transcripts are involved in Piwil1 nucleolar localization.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 expresses concern about this mechanism: 'the ability to reduce PiwiL1 in the nucleolus through polI inhibition with actD and BMH-21 is surprising. What drives the accumulation of PiwiL1 in the nucleolus then if in the meioc mutant there is less transcription anyway?' This logical inconsistency raises questions about whether pre-rRNA transcripts drive Piwil1 localization or are merely associated with it.

results.result: Piwil1 interacts with transcriptional silencing proteins Setdb1 and HP1α (detected by co-IP and pull-down), both localize to nucleoli in 1-2 cell spermatogonia, and show higher nucleolar levels in meioc mutants, suggesting Piwil1 recruits these silencing factors to nucleoli.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the protein-protein interaction data. Reviewer 2 states 'Piwil1 interacts with transcriptional silencers that repress rRNA transcription' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors nicely provided the molecular evidence on the antagonism of Meioc to Piwil1 in the rRNA synthesis, which supported by the genetic evidence.' The co-IP and localization data are not challenged.

results.result: ChIP analysis shows meioc mutants have higher enrichment of H3K9me3 and Piwil1 at rDNA loci compared to wild-type, while piwil1 heterozygotes show decreased enrichment, correlating nucleolar Piwil1 levels with repressive chromatin marks at rDNA.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 expresses skepticism: 'the de-enrichment of H3K9me3 in the heterozygous (Figure 6F) is very modest and in my opinion not convincingly different relative to the control provided.' This suggests the ChIP data showing reduced H3K9me3 in piwil1+/- may not be robust enough to strongly support the dose-dependent relationship between Piwil1 and H3K9me3.

results.result: Genetic reduction of Piwil1 in piwil1+/- heterozygotes upregulates 28S rRNA, and piwil1+/-;meioc-/- double mutants show partial rescue of the meioc phenotype with increased rRNA, recovery of differentiation to 32-cell stage, and increased 4-8 cell cyst ratios approaching wild-type levels.
results.evaluation: All reviewers strongly affirm this genetic interaction. Reviewer 1 states 'the genetic compensation of meioc mutant phenotypes (both organismal and molecular) through reduction in PiwiL1 levels are evidence for a direct role for PiwiL1 in mediating the phenotypes of meioc mutant.' Reviewer 3 notes this is 'supported by the genetic evidence that the inability of the meioc mutant to enter meiosis is suppressed by the piwil1 heterozygosity.'

results.result: ythdc2 knockout zebrafish arrest at 8-cell spermatogonia but maintain normal 4-8/1-2 cell cyst ratios and normal rRNA populations (unlike meioc mutants), and show no Piwil1 nucleolar accumulation, indicating Meioc functions independently of Ythdc2 in regulating early spermatogonial differentiation and rRNA upregulation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding. Reviewer 2 explicitly notes 'In mouse, the Meioc knockout phenocopies the Ythdc2 knockout...Here, in zebrafish, Meioc has acquired a Ythdc2-independent function.' The differential phenotypes between meioc and ythdc2 mutants are not challenged and support the independence of Meioc function.

results.result: Small RNA sequencing shows similar overall abundance in meioc mutants vs heterozygotes, with decreased rRNA-derived small RNAs (likely due to reduced rRNA expression), suggesting Meioc does not critically affect small RNA generation.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 finds this 'confounding': 'I would have assumed that the interaction of PiwiL1 with the rRNA is mediated through small RNAs but the reduction in numbers do not support this model. But perhaps it is simply a redistribution of small RNAs that is occurring.' This indicates uncertainty about whether the small RNA data truly rules out piRNA involvement in the mechanism.

results.result: In isolated sox17::egfp spermatogonia, Meioc expression ranges from undetectable to >51 granules (with nuclear localization only in 51≤ cells); 28S rRNA intensity increases with 11-50+ Meioc granules; Piwil1 levels are constant across cells; nucleolar Piwil1 is observed in cells with 11-50 Meioc granules but not 51≤ granules, supporting that Meioc inhibits Piwil1 nucleolar localization to enable rRNA upregulation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this correlative analysis. Reviewer 3 notes 'the authors nicely address my previous points' suggesting earlier concerns about this relationship were resolved. The single-cell correlation data linking Meioc levels to rRNA and Piwil1 localization is not challenged.

results.result: The overall model proposes that Meioc has a unique function in preventing Piwil1 nucleolar localization, thereby allowing rRNA transcription upregulation and promoting SSC differentiation; zebrafish SSCs maintain low rRNA transcription in their undifferentiated state, contrasting with many other stem cell types.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the overall model. Reviewer 1 states 'overall I find this paper to be solid and valuable, providing evidence for a consistent link between PIWI systems and ribosomal biogenesis.' Reviewer 2 calls it 'a fundamental study that expands our understanding of how ribosome biogenesis contributes to differentiation.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'the authors provide convincing evidence that Meioc antagonizes Piwil1.' However, mechanistic details remain uncertain (see C5, C129-C133).

results.result: The study concludes that zebrafish SSCs maintain low rRNA transcription with repressive marks similar to Drosophila piRNA targets of Pol II (not typical high RiBi of ES/Drosophila GSCs), representing a conserved Argonaute function in controlling ribosome biogenesis, with zebrafish Piwil1 using analogous silencing machinery (Setdb1, HP1α, H3K9me3) as Drosophila Piwi uses for Pol II transcription.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these comparative conclusions. Reviewer 1 notes the results 'provide evidence for a consistent link between PIWI systems and ribosomal biogenesis' and that findings are 'likely to be of interest to people in the community.' Reviewer 2 states this 'expands our understanding' and 'identifies a new role for Piwil1 in directing transcriptional silencing of rDNA.' The evolutionary comparisons are not challenged.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C32, C51, C52, C54, C60. Both evaluations find the phenotypic characterization of meioc mutants compelling and well-supported by histology, marker expression, and cell counts showing failure to differentiate beyond early spermatogonia.

Perfect agreement on claims C61, C62, C63, C64, C71. Both evaluations accept the OP-Puro and cycloheximide data demonstrating that upregulated protein synthesis is required for spermatogonial differentiation. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C72, C73, C75-C81. Both evaluations find the in situ hybridization, fluorescence quantification, and RT-qPCR data convincingly demonstrate rRNA upregulation during differentiation and its absence in mutants.

Perfect agreement on claims C84, C85, C86. Both evaluations accept the Northern blot data showing reduced rRNA transcription but intact processing in meioc mutants. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C89, C90, C91, C92. Both evaluations accept the bisulfite sequencing data showing increased DNA methylation at rDNA loci in meioc mutants as part of the epigenetic silencing mechanism.

Perfect agreement on claims C3, C4, C104-C115. Both evaluations strongly support the Meioc-Piwil1 interaction and Piwil1 relocalization to nucleoli in meioc mutants, confirmed by immunofluorescence, co-IP, and domain mapping.

Disagreement on claims C5, C129-C133. OpenEval finds the RIP-qPCR and inhibitor data supportive, noting the mechanism remains correlative. Peer reviewers express concern about the logical inconsistency: if meioc mutants have less rRNA transcription, why would Pol I inhibition reduce Piwil1 nucleolar localization? This questions whether pre-rRNA drives Piwil1 localization.

Perfect agreement on claims C146-C155. Both evaluations accept the single-cell correlation data linking Meioc expression levels to rRNA upregulation and inverse relationship with nucleolar Piwil1, though both note the analysis is correlative.

Strong agreement on claims C95-C102 regarding meioc vs ythdc2 mutant comparisons. Both evaluations accept that the data demonstrate functional independence of Meioc from Ythdc2 in early spermatogonial stages, supporting a zebrafish-specific Meioc function.

Perfect agreement on claims C6, C7, C120-C128. Both evaluations strongly affirm the genetic interaction data showing partial rescue of meioc mutant phenotypes by reducing Piwil1, providing compelling evidence for the antagonistic relationship.

Agreement on claims C8, C9, C135-C137, C141-C145 regarding Piwil1 interactions with silencing machinery. Both evaluations accept the co-IP and ChIP data. However, peer review (R9) expresses skepticism about the dose-dependent H3K9me3 enrichment in piwil1+/- (C138-C140), finding the de-enrichment 'very modest' and not convincingly different.

Disagreement on claims C117, C118, C119. OpenEval finds the small RNA sequencing data reasonably supports that Meioc does not critically affect small RNA generation. Peer reviewers find this 'confounding' and express uncertainty about whether the data truly rules out piRNA involvement in the mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C12-C14, C43-C45, C49, C170-C171 regarding the overall model. Both evaluations affirm the main conclusions are well-supported by collective evidence, though both note some mechanistic details remain uncertain (particularly regarding how Meioc prevents Piwil1 nucleolar localization).

Partial disagreement on claims C10, C11. OpenEval finds the ChIP-qPCR data showing increased H3K9me3 at rDNA in meioc mutants supportive. Peer reviewers express skepticism about the robustness of the dose-dependent relationship in piwil1+/- heterozygotes (related claims C138-C140).

Agreement on claims C163, C164 (and related C12, C156-C157, C186-C187). Both evaluations accept the summary statements and comparative conclusions about PIWI systems and ribosomal biogenesis, finding the work expands understanding of these mechanisms.
Agreement on claims C157, C186, C187 regarding discussion points and evolutionary comparisons. Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited and reasonable interpretations in broader context.
